topic: Conflicting official rules on when a skipped annual increase becomes 'banked'
finding: Rule 4.12(a) says 'A full 12 months must have elapsed'; the current sf.gov 'Banked rent increases' page says 'A skipped increase is only banked if at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase'. Both are official SF Rent Board sources. The worked examples on sf.gov 'Learn about rent increases' and 'Increasing rents during irregular periods' follow the 12-month logic.
impact: Changes Unit 2's maximum lawful increase from 13.1% to 11.7% and changes whether the June 1, 2025 1.4% is preserved. Do not serve a banked-increase notice before this is resolved.
action: Ask a Rent Board counselor for the current interpretation and have a California tenant-side attorney review the calculation. Both scenarios are shown on the Units page.

topic: Conflicting official dates for when the license requirement began
finding: Sec. 37.15(c) and Rule 13.14 say 7/1/2022 (10+ units) and 3/1/2023 (condos / <10 units). Official Form 538 (2024-25 Bond Measure Worksheet) states 7/1/2020 and 3/1/2021. The sf.gov Housing Inventory pages and the noncompliance notice use the 2022/2023 dates.
impact: Could affect the review of PAST increases. For any NEW increase, the practical rule is the same: a current license must be on file on the effective date.
action: Use the ordinance/Rule 13.14 dates; ask the Rent Board to reconcile Form 538 if reviewing older increases.

topic: Tension between Sec. 37.15(e) and Rule 13.14 on the remedy for an unlicensed increase
finding: Sec. 37.15(e) says 'a tenant shall not be obligated to pay the increased rent for months during the period of suspension'; Rule 13.14 says the 'entire rent increase [is] null and void'. The sf.gov noncompliance notice says it 'may be null and void' and that a refund may be due (possibly for multiple years).
impact: Affects refund exposure if any past increase was imposed without a license.
action: Have counsel review the full rent history and license status for each past effective date.

topic: 2027-2028 allowable increase rate is not published
finding: No official source consulted contains the rate effective March 1, 2027 - February 28, 2028. The Rent Board also documented that the U.S. Department of Labor did not publish October 2025 CPI data and considered temporary alternate CPI methodologies for the 3/1/2026 and 3/1/2027 rates.
impact: Any increase effective on/after March 1, 2027 cannot be calculated yet. Value left blank on the Rates page.
action: Recheck the official Current Rates page before choosing an effective date in 2027.

topic: Rent Board's online Ordinance is not the official legal record
finding: The Rent Board's own Rent Ordinance page states: 'The Rent Board's version of the Rent Ordinance is not the official record of the laws or regulations of the City and County of San Francisco. It is provided for administrative and public convenience only.'
impact: Section text quoted in this project comes from the Rent Board's convenience copy, not the certified official record.
action: For any filing or dispute, verify the operative text with the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors / City Attorney or counsel.

topic: Third-party sources conflict with the official licensing sequence
finding: Non-official landlord guides state variously that an owner must 'apply for' a license, that notice comes before the license, or that 60-day notice applies to >=10% increases. Official sf.gov says the license is automatically generated by reporting, that no petition is needed for annual/banked increases, that the license must be current on the effective date, and that 90 days (not 60) applies above 10%.
impact: Relying on third-party guidance could produce an unenforceable notice.
action: Use only the official sf.gov and California Legislative Information links in the Sources page. No non-official source is used as verification anywhere in this project.

finding: Build year (1940), rent-controlled status, building unit count, occupancy/lease dates, rent amounts, tenant composition, and the absence of any prior rent increase are owner-provided. No lease, assessor record, or Portal record was consulted.
impact: Coverage, the anniversary date, banking eligibility, and license status all depend on these facts.
action: Verify build date on the official Property Information Map, verify license status for each relevant year in the Rent Board Portal, and confirm the rent history from leases and notices.

topic: Unit 1: April 1, 2026 occupant change and the 12-month clock
finding: One original occupant still resides there, so no market-rate reset is available and no increase may be based on the new occupant. But whether April 1, 2026 created a genuinely new tenancy for the 12-month clock is an unverified fact. If it did, the first increase could be no earlier than April 1, 2027 - a period whose rate is not yet published.
impact: Determines the earliest lawful effective date for Unit 1.
action: Confirm with the lease documents, a Rent Board counselor, and counsel. Do not reset the rent.

topic: Unit 1: status of the February 1, 2026 skipped 1.4% increase
finding: It is unknown whether an increase was imposed on/after February 1, 2026. Official Rent Board examples show a skipped increase can be permanently lost when the effective date moves, and the 12/24-month banking conflict applies.
impact: Affects whether any banked amount may be added for Unit 1.
action: Confirm the rent history in writing; do not assume the 1.4% was preserved.

topic: Unit 2: choosing an off-anniversary effective date
finding: Banked increases are cleanest on the June 1 anniversary date. An effective date on another day can permanently lose an available increase and creates a new anniversary date; an effective date on/after March 1, 2027 would need the unpublished 2027-28 rate. Banked totals above 10% also require 90 days' notice.
impact: Timing and notice period are interdependent here.
action: Model the effective date against the 90-day notice requirement and the unpublished 2027 rate before serving anything.

finding: The owner asked that personal information be kept internal only and that published data use placeholder names while dates and amounts stay the same. Because this is a PUBLIC GitHub repository and a public GitHub Pages site, no real tenant names or initials were stored anywhere in the repository; only Occupant A-F placeholders appear.
impact: The published site cannot be linked back to individual tenants. Dates and dollar amounts are preserved exactly as provided.
action: Owner review: confirm whether any internal (non-public) record containing the original identifiers should exist outside this repository.

finding: Federal numeric rent cap for private unsubsidized housing; official 94122-specific market benchmark; official model rent-increase notice wording; official record-retention period; 2027-28 allowable rate; current license status; building unit count; whether a new tenancy began April 1, 2026; whether any prior increase was imposed; whether any official source requires raising both units; whether a tenant lawyer will approve an increase; internal corporate rent-setting practices; the specific list of additional SF-local protected classes beyond state law.
impact: These cells are blank on the site by design; no value was inferred or filled in.
action: See the Flagged for Review page for each item and its official governing link. Supply or verify only from an official source.

finding: Initial commit b747350 contained only README.md ('# RentincreaseSF5'). There was no pre-existing research, data, site, COORDINATION.md, or prior findings to review line by line.
impact: All content in this project is newly created and newly verified in this session.
action: No action; review the Sources and Verification pages.

finding: This is research and compliance documentation built only from official government sources. It is not legal advice, does not determine the lawful rent for either unit, and does not substitute for a Rent Board counselor or a California attorney. The Rent Board itself states it cannot give legal advice.
impact: Any final notice should be reviewed by counsel before service.
action: Use the free Rent Board counseling line and the official referral listing for case-specific advice.

topic: Official City fair-housing PDF section could not be retrieved line by line
finding: The City's Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice (2020-2025) lists Section IV.A.10 'Other State/Local Protected Classes' in its table of contents, but the PDF parser made only the first 30 pages available, so the section text was not verified. An earlier draft of this project listed 'creed, height, place of birth, weight' as local classes from that document; that specific list could NOT be verified and has been removed.
impact: The site now uses only the verified state-law protected classes from Government Code 12955 and leaves any additional local classes blank.
action: Owner review: consult the SF Human Rights Commission or the full City document for the current local protected-class list; do not rely on an unverified list.
